name: Light Vinaceous-Fawn
lede: Light Vinaceous-Fawn is a paler step off [[vinaceous-fawn|Vinaceous-Fawn]], a muted pink-brown Ridgway named in his 1912 "vinaceous" family of wine-tinged naturalist colors.

sections.title: A modifier on a wine-tinged brown
sections.body:
The name is built by grammar: "light" over the parent [[vinaceous-fawn|Vinaceous-Fawn]], itself named from *vinaceus*, wine-colored, combined with fawn, a young deer's coat color [1]. Ridgway's 1912 atlas plates this lighter step at plate XL, hue 13''', tone d, and ISCC-NBS separately filed it in 1955 as block 33 [1]. Measured, it is lighter and notably less saturated than its parent (lightness 75 against 65, chroma 14 against 22) [1].

Its nearest named neighbor is [[sweet-pea|Sweet Pea]], 3.3 units away, almost the same, with [[light-brownish-vinaceous|Light Brownish-Vinaceous]] close behind at 4.2, redder [1].

sections.title: Field notes
sections.body: Our archive finds this pale pink-brown in 381 of 23,781 paintings (1.6 percent, as photographed), more common than 74 percent of the named colors we track [2]. It most often plays a hidden color, in 47 percent of its strongest matches; John Singer Sargent carries it in 6 of his 287 works here, and it is most over-represented in paintings from India, at 2.5 times the expected rate [2]. The earliest dated match runs to 900, by Zhao Guangfu, 1,012 years before Ridgway's 1912 record; a floor, not a first, since the archive's early centuries are thin [2].

origin.named_after: a descriptive modifier: light + Vinaceous-Fawn (from Latin vinaceus, "wine-colored", plus fawn)
